summary: Finland is permissive for the roof rat, now confirmed in writing by the Finnish authorities (June 2026). Keeping rats as companion or hobby animals needs NO permit or registration under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 (specified for small companion and hobby animals by Government Decree 674/2010). There is currently no list of allowed or denied species (one may come later), and Rattus rattus is on neither the EU invasive Union list (Reg. 1143/2014) nor Finland's national invasive list (Decree 1725/2015), so no species-specific ban applies; the Finnish Environment Institute confirmed it is not a CITES species. The only requirement is a NOTIFICATION of activity (not a permit) at commercial scale: selling or handing over small companion animals from at least 7 cages, terraria, or aquaria in regular use, or merely keeping them at 20 or more (Animal Welfare Act Appendix 2). A wild, living-in-the-wild animal may not be taken into possession (captive-bred is fine). Import from another EU country follows standard pet-movement rules; a third-country (for example US) import is handled by the Food Authority's border-control team. Never release.
agency_confirmations: Finnish Food Authority (Ruokavirasto), Animal Health and Welfare, written reply June 2026: keeping rats as companion or hobby animals requires no permit or registration under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 (specified by Government Decree 674/2010). There is currently no list of species allowed or denied as companion animals. A notification of activity is required only at commercial scale: selling or handing over small companion animals (self-bred or not) from at least 7 cages, terraria, or aquaria in regular use, or keeping them at 20 or more (Animal Welfare Act Appendix 2). A wild, living-in-the-wild vertebrate may not be taken into possession.
Finnish Environment Institute (Syke), CITES authority, written reply June 2026: Rattus rattus is not a CITES species and has no CITES requirements.

Finnish Food Authority, import/export, June 2026: movement of pet rodents within the EU, Norway, and Switzerland follows the standard import/export rules; a third-country import (for example from the United States) is handled by the Food Authority's border-control team under the usual rabbit-and-rodent import requirements.

keep.why: The Finnish Food Authority confirmed (June 2026) that keeping rats as companion or hobby animals requires no permit or registration under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 (specified by Government Decree 674/2010). There is currently no allowed/denied species list. A notification of activity is required only if you keep small companion animals at a large scale (at least 20 cages, terraria, or aquaria in regular use). A captive-bred roof rat is fine; a wild, living-in-the-wild animal may not be taken into possession.
keep.governing_law: Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 + Government Decree 674/2010 (no permit to keep; notification at >=20 cages, Appendix 2). Finnish Food Authority written reply, June 2026.

breed.why: No breeding permit is required. The Finnish Food Authority confirmed (June 2026) that selling or handing over small companion animals from a self-bred litter triggers only a NOTIFICATION of activity (not a permit), and only at scale: at least 7 cages, terraria, or aquaria in regular use. A hobbyist breeding below that threshold needs nothing beyond the Animal Welfare Act's general duties.
breed.governing_law: Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 + Decree 674/2010; notification at >=7 cages for selling self-bred (Appendix 2). Finnish Food Authority, June 2026.

sell_give.why: No dealer permit is required. Selling, handing over, or conveying small companion animals (self-bred or not) triggers only a NOTIFICATION of activity at scale: at least 7 cages, terraria, or aquaria in regular use (Finnish Food Authority, June 2026). Below that, giving or selling a roof rat needs no notification. Free gifting is treated the same way.
sell_give.governing_law: Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 + Decree 674/2010; notification at >=7 cages for selling/handing over (Appendix 2). Finnish Food Authority, June 2026.

transport.why: Rattus rattus is not a CITES species (Finnish Environment Institute, June 2026), so no CITES paperwork applies. Movement within the EU follows the standard pet-movement rules. A third-country (for example US) import is handled by the Finnish Food Authority's border-control team and follows the usual rabbits-and-rodents import requirements (health/veterinary), not a species-specific bar. Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: No CITES (Syke, June 2026); EU pet-movement rules; Finnish Food Authority third-country import requirements (rabbits and rodents).

restrictions.summary: Keeping, breeding or transferring rats at scale requires a NOTIFICATION (ilmoitus) to Ruokavirasto at least 30 days before you start: at 7 or more cages, terraria or aquaria in regular use this counts as professional/commercial activity, and at 20 or more as large-scale non-professional keeping. Below those thresholds, hobby keeping/breeding/rehoming is unregistered, subject only to the welfare standards. Filing puts the premises in the keeper register and open to welfare inspection. The threshold is the same for the fancy rat (R. norvegicus). Never release a roof rat.
steps: If at or above 7 cages (professional) or 20 cages (large-scale), file the ilmoitus to Ruokavirasto via the animal-keeper and facility register at least 30 days before commencing
Below the threshold, keep no notification is required; meet the Decree 674/2010 welfare and housing standards
restrictions.where_to_file: Ruokavirasto (Finnish Food Authority), via the animal-keeper and facility register (eläintenpitäjä- ja pitopaikkarekisteri)

restrictions.summary: Government Decree 674/2010 sets minimum housing for the rat (rotta) generically, with no distinction between R. rattus and R. norvegicus: a minimum cage floor area and height, additional floor area per group-housed animal, a continuous nest box / shelter for concealment, species-suitable substrate for digging and foraging, continuous fresh water, and a balanced diet. Falling below these is an animal welfare offence. No microchipping or registration of pet rodents is required.

inquiry_focus: (1) Is Rattus rattus (mustarotta/kattorotta) subject to any restriction under Finland's national invasive alien species decree (1725/2015) or Finland's implementation of EU Reg. 1143/2014 that would restrict keeping it as a pet, i.e., is it on the national list or not? (2) Under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023, does the ilmoituksenvarainen eläintenpito notification for small hobby rodents such as rats trigger at 7 cages (professional) or 20 cages (large-scale), is it filed to Ruokavirasto, and is anything beyond notification required? (3) For non-commercial movement of captive-bred R. rattus from another EU member state by the owner personally, are there any species-specific documentation or health-certificate requirements?
